LOCAL GOVERNMENT ROUNDUP

Area school boards and local villages kept busy this past week with budget planning, land-use decisions, and personnel matters. Most meetings this cycle are agenda-only, so outcomes remain pending.

  • The Wausau School Board was set to approve its 2026-2027 budget and tax levy at its September 14 regular meeting, based on a projected 4.03% increase in equalized property values.
  • The Wausau School Board convened in closed session September 21 to hold a pupil expulsion hearing, with action on the matter taken if deemed necessary and appropriate.
  • The Kronenwetter Village Board was set to vote September 14 on a zoning change for a Lea Road property and on a WPDES Memorandum of Agreement, and to appoint an interim village clerk.
  • Kronenwetter's Administrative Policy Committee was scheduled September 15 to review a 2027 operating budget preview and a 10-year capital improvement plan update.
  • The Weston Plan Commission was set September 14 to review a preliminary condominium plat on Camp Phillips Road and consider possible action on conditional use permit violations at three properties.
  • The DC Everest School Board was scheduled September 16 to approve staff employment changes, health insurance renewal, and Act 89 implementation details for the 2026-2027 school year.

Coming up: Tuesday, September 22 is a full day for Marathon County and Wausau city government, with the County Board meeting at 7 p.m., the City's Finance Committee at 5:15 p.m., and the Board of Public Works and Community Development Authority meeting earlier in the day. Also Monday, the Kronenwetter Plan Commission takes up a land division request and the Green Tree Trails Subdivision plat at 6 p.m., and Weston's Board of Trustees meets at 6 p.m.
